sections.title: What transfers and what stays behind
sections.body: Moving accounting software is not a simple copy and paste. Your master data transfers easily. You can export your customers, vendors and item lists from your current system and import them into Paper & Pen using a spreadsheet. However, historical documents like past invoices, bills and receipts do not move over. You must keep your old records for tax compliance. The most practical approach is to switch at the start of a new financial year or quarter. You close your books in the old system, extract your trial balance, and enter those figures as opening balances in Paper & Pen via journal entries.
items: Export and import your customer and vendor lists
Transfer your item catalogue and pricing via spreadsheet
Historical transactions remain in your old system
Enter opening balances using manual journal entries

sections.title: What you gain with Paper & Pen
sections.body: Paper & Pen provides a straightforward platform for managing your daily operations. The core sales and invoicing features are entirely free. You can create quotations, track leads, issue invoices and record payments without a subscription. The system supports multiple currencies and configurable tax rates. Your team can operate the software in English, Arabic, Hindi, Bengali or Urdu. If your business grows, you can add paid modules for HR and payroll or manufacturing and bills of materials. This modular approach means you only pay for complex features when your operations actually require them.
items: Free core invoicing, quotations and sales tracking
Five interface languages including right-to-left Arabic
Share documents directly via email or WhatsApp link
Optional paid modules for HR and manufacturing

sections.title: Who should remain on Zoho Books
sections.body: Paper & Pen is not the right choice for every business. Zoho Books is an established accounting platform with a paid subscription model. You should check their official website for current plans and pricing. If your business relies heavily on the wider ecosystem of Zoho applications, moving your accounting software will break those connections. Companies that require automatic bank feed imports, open-banking connections, or a vast marketplace of third-party app integrations should stay where they are. If your current software handles complex, automated workflows that your team depends on daily, a switch will likely cause unnecessary disruption.
items: Businesses heavily integrated into a wider software suite
Companies requiring automatic bank feed imports
Teams relying on third-party app marketplaces
Organisations with highly complex automated workflows

faqs.q: Can I import my old invoices into Paper & Pen?
faqs.a: No. Historical documents like past invoices, receipts and purchase orders do not transfer between accounting systems. You must retain access to your previous software or download PDF copies of your historical records for tax compliance. You will start fresh in Paper & Pen by entering your unpaid invoices as opening balances.

faqs.q: When is the best time to migrate my accounting software?
faqs.a: The most practical time to switch is at the beginning of a new financial year. If that is too far away, choose the start of a new quarter or month. This clean break allows you to close your accounts in your old system, generate a final trial balance, and enter those exact figures as opening balances in your new software.

faqs.q: How do I handle unpaid invoices during the transition?
faqs.a: You have two options for open invoices. You can leave them in your old system and record the payments there until they are cleared. Alternatively, you can recreate the outstanding invoices in Paper & Pen so you can track all future payments in one place. Most businesses prefer recreating open invoices to centralise their collections.

faqs.q: Does Paper & Pen connect to my bank account?
faqs.a: No. Paper & Pen does not support automatic bank feeds or open-banking connections. You must enter your bank transactions manually or upload them if supported. If your business processes hundreds of small bank transactions daily and relies on automatic bank reconciliation, you should carefully consider if a manual process fits your operations.
